parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Make reusable learning inspectable
parts.body:
A community of practice helps teams share tested methods across business units without making a central team deliver every project. It needs more than enthusiasm. Give each published pattern an owner, version, intended use, evaluation evidence, known limits, and a contact for questions. Record failed approaches as carefully as successful ones. A prompt that worked for one language and data set should not be copied into another service without testing.

Champions can demonstrate workflows, collect problems, and connect colleagues with specialists. They should not become an informal approval authority. Keep policy, data access, security, and release decisions with named owners. The community should make those routes easier to understand and reveal where they are too slow or confusing. NIST's governance framework calls for documented roles, communication, and feedback across the AI lifecycle.

Choose a small set of shared artifacts: a use-case entry, evaluation template, failure example, release checklist, and incident lesson. A searchable library with dates and owners is more useful than an unmoderated collection of screenshots. Retire patterns when models, policy, or source data change.

example.title: A filled pattern card
example.body: Illustrative card: Contract clause retrieval, version 2. Owner: Legal Operations lead. Intended use: internal analysts locate clauses for human review; it makes no contractual decision. Data: the approved contract repository under each analyst's existing access; customer documents cannot cross accounts. Evidence: 116 of 120 representative queries returned a correct cited clause, including amendment cases; the four failures involved scanned annexes. A wrong clause in a signed advice memo is a material error, so the team excludes scans pending a separate test. Operating owner: legal product lead; incident contact: platform on-call. Last review: 3 September 2026; review again after a source, model, access rule, or policy change. Another unit must validate its own permissions, corpus, language, and error criterion. The result and date are invented for teaching.

exercise.title: Publish one pattern
exercise.body: Create a pattern card for a workflow you know. Include intended users, data boundary, owner, evaluation result, failure mode, review date, and what a second team must test before reuse.

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Run a clinic that produces decisions
parts.body:
A monthly clinic can pair one useful result with one failure. Ask each presenter to show the original baseline, intended users, evaluation method, observed outcome, user feedback, cost, and next decision. Give the audience time to challenge case mix, downstream correction, and limits to reuse. Publish the corrected account afterward with a responsible owner. A polished demo without denominators teaches little.

An internal knowledge assistant might reduce search time for one team's policy documents. Another team should ask whether it has comparable source quality and permission boundaries. The clinic can connect them to the platform and data owners, but it cannot confer authorization by applause. If a failure involved exposing restricted material, share a sanitized account that explains the mechanism and control change without repeating the sensitive content.

Track what happened after the meeting. Did another team adapt and validate the pattern? Did a repeated problem lead to a shared platform fix? Did a supposed success lose its benefit in production? These are more meaningful measures than attendance alone.

example.title: A clinic decision log
example.body: Illustrative 14 October clinic entry: finance assistant's weekly report use grew to 80 of 100 eligible reports, yet 6 of 80 used last year's policy after an update. The presentation showed the outdated source, six affected drafts, a corrected retrieval test, and a manual fallback. Decision: pause the pattern for finance until all six are reviewed and 40 seeded current-policy cases pass with no material stale citation. Owner: Finance product lead; platform owner fixes source refresh by 21 October; evaluation lead retests by 23 October. Other units receive a library notice and must check whether they share the source. The dates and acceptance rule are illustrative.

exercise.title: Set the clinic agenda
exercise.body: Design a 45-minute clinic with a successful use, a failed use, a structured challenge, and a decision log. Require one concrete follow-up owner and date from each presentation. State what sensitive details cannot be shared.

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Keep the community connected to controls
parts.body:
Give champions a charter: help colleagues find approved tools, collect questions, demonstrate evaluated patterns, and route concerns to the correct owner. The charter should list what they cannot approve. Provide office hours with product, security, privacy, data, and evaluation specialists. A rotating expert can answer common questions while preserving a written escalation path for consequential decisions.

Review the library quarterly. An owner checks each pattern against current models, data, policy, and incidents. Mark it current, restricted, or retired. Record reuse with the adapting team's own test result; copying a prompt is not evidence that the new use is safe. For operations across Canada and EU countries, attach language, data, and jurisdiction limits to the pattern so local teams see what remains to validate. A local data steward must approve the source and permissions; the product release owner accepts the local test under the organization's risk process.

Measure the learning loop with denominators: validated adoptions out of attempted transfers, patterns reviewed on time out of patterns due, and defects fixed within the agreed interval out of defects reported. Also record median time for a team to find a relevant tested pattern from a sample of searches, and outcomes after reuse. These measures are suggested operating practices, not NIST or OECD mandates. Do not reward a low incident count that encourages silence; early reports can expose a defect before release.

example.title: A local permission gate
example.body: A Canadian service unit requests a French and English answer checker built for an internal help desk. The local data steward checks repository permissions and purpose; the privacy and security owners review the new access pattern under their authority. The product owner prepares 60 local cases, including French exceptions, and sets an illustrative acceptance criterion of zero material unsupported advice. Four cases fail because the local policy corpus uses different terms. The release owner rejects the transfer, assigns source mapping to the local team, and schedules a retest. The central champion can share the defect with other users but cannot approve access or release.

exercise.title: Write a champion charter
exercise.body: List a champion's permitted actions, prohibited approvals, office-hour support, escalation contacts, protected time, and measures of useful contribution. Add a quarterly review rule for stale patterns.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: roles, monitoring, and feedback

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Scale a lesson across units
parts.body:
Suppose one team has a successful internal document assistant and two other teams want it. Ask the origin team for its evaluation set, source boundaries, integration design, costs, and incident history. Ask each adopting team for its user group, document quality, access rules, language needs, and workflow baseline. The shared platform may carry over; the benefit and risk evidence must be checked in each setting.

Approve a transfer in stages. First, test the pattern on local representative cases. Next, run a small supervised deployment with corrections and user feedback. Then decide whether to scale based on quality, cost, and operational readiness. The origin team can coach and share artifacts, while each adopting product owner remains accountable for its outcome. Record changes so the library reflects both the common design and local departures.

If the receiving team finds a defect, route it back to the pattern owner and other users. That feedback loop is how a community improves the shared method. The executive sponsor should fund moderation, expert time, and maintenance; voluntary enthusiasm alone is a fragile operating plan.

example.title: A failed transfer and its feedback
example.body: Procurement tries to adapt HR's document search pattern. Its data steward approves only its own supplier repository and existing user permissions. In a 50-case local test, 7 table questions return incomplete citations because supplier attachments are scanned. The product owner had set at most one material citation error as the illustrative gate. The release owner rejects rollout, funds extraction and a retest, and logs 1 attempted transfer, 0 validated adoptions, and 1 reported defect. The pattern owner adds 'scanned tables untested' to the library; other users receive the notice. HR's result remains scoped to its own documents.

exercise.title: Create a transfer plan
exercise.body: For a pattern moving from one unit to another, write the origin evidence, local differences, test sample, control review, pilot boundary, owner, and go/no-go criterion. Include one mechanism for reporting a defect back to all current users.
